content.text:
## Summary

**Defects found:**
1. The page used generic `<div>`s for every region (top bar, main content, hours panel, footer) with no semantic landmarks, so screen reader users had no way to jump between the nav, main content, and footer regions (WCAG 1.3.1).
2. The in-page anchor links ("Visit" → `#visit`, "Events" → `#events`) pointed at non-focusable targets (an `<h1>` and a plain `<div>`), so activating them via mouse or keyboard scrolled the page but never moved focus or gave assistive tech any indication that context had changed.

Note: the two nav links themselves were already real `<a href>` elements, so they were natively keyboard-operable (focusable, Enter-activated, and correctly bubbling into the existing click-tracking instrumentation) — no change was needed there, and I left that mouse/keyboard path untouched.

**Changes made (all in `index.html`):**
- `.top` div → `<header>`, the links wrapper `<span>` → `<nav aria-label="Primary">`, `.hours` div → `<section>` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading, `.bottom` div → `<footer>`, and wrapped the hero + hours content in `<main>`. This gives AT users real landmarks to navigate by, with no visual change (these elements are block-level/flex-item by default, and all existing class-based CSS selectors still apply unchanged).
- Added `tabindex="-1"` to the `#visit` heading and the `#events` section so that activating the corresponding nav link (by mouse or keyboard) moves focus to the target, giving screen readers an announcement of the new content and putting the keyboard tab order in the right place — matching what the mouse path visually does.
- Gave the "This week" heading an `id` (`hours-heading`) purely to label the new `<section>` via `aria-labelledby`.

**Left alone:**
- All `data-track` attributes, `id`s, visible text, colors/layout, and the click-tracking script — untouched.
- Contrast ratios for all text/background pairs were checked (nav links, hero copy, hours copy, footer copy) and all exceed 4.5:1, so no color changes were needed.
- No custom widgets exist on this page (only two real links), so there was nothing to convert to/from ARIA-patched divs.
